claims.d: SECI received the largest parcel (23,000 ha). On 2023-07-17 it sought permission for hybrid projects (wind-only being unviable) and in July 2023 surrendered the whole parcel 'following instructions from the renewable energy minister' (Scroll/Guardian).
claims.upgradeIf: SECI board minutes / MNRE letter opened

claims.lab: Khavda: NTPC 9,500 ha / 4,750 MW
claims.d: NTPC (via NTPC REL) allotted 9,500 ha for 4,750 MW; 212.5 MW installed per the Wikipedia table. Other allottees: Sarjan Realities 9,500 ha/4,750 MW; GSECL 6,650 ha/3,325 MW; GIPCL 4,750 ha/2,375 MW.

claims.lab: Khavda: Adani Power named park developer for surrendered SECI land (24 Aug 2023), no bidding on record
claims.d: Adani requested 23,000 ha for wind-solar hybrid on 2023-07-03 citing the 'revised extant policy/guidelines', revised to 25,500 ha on 2023-07-07 (before SECI's formal 2023-07-17 request and July surrender); the CM's high-powered committee selected Adani Power as park developer on 2023-08-24 without documented competitive bidding. Adani thereafter holds ~445 sq km, more than all other developers combined.
claims.upgradeIf: Committee minutes show no alternative applicants or no notice; RTI shows lease terms below the SECI offer
claims.killIf: A public call for developers or a competitive process for the surrendered land is produced

benefit.how: Control of the land needed to realise the 30 GW park; capacity potential of the border strip rose from ~1,100 MW to ~10,000 MW after the MoD relaxation

claims.lab: Adani: 'fully compliant'; allocation 'adheres to policy guidelines'
claims.d: Adani Group statement to Scroll/Guardian: the project is 'fully compliant with all … laws and regulations' with 'necessary approvals from … competent authorities'; the land allocation 'adheres to policy guidelines'. MoD, Gujarat government, MNRE and SECI had not responded to the reporters' questions at publication.

claims.lab: MoD relaxes border-zone limits for RE (21 Apr / 8 May 2023)
claims.d: A 2023-04-21 MoD meeting approved wind turbines 1–2 km and hybrid plants 2–8 km from the border; guidelines of 2023-05-08 permit RE plants up to 20 km from the India–Pakistan border in consultation with MoD. Retired officers criticised the security trade-off.

claims.lab: Sequence test: rule change → Adani request (3 Jul) → SECI surrender (Jul) → Adani selected (24 Aug)
claims.d: Adani's first request for the SECI parcel (2023-07-03) cites the revised guidelines and precedes SECI's own hybrid request (2023-07-17) and surrender; selection followed within seven weeks. The chronology is consistent with foreknowledge of the surrender, but equally with an applicant reading a public MoD guideline and asking first.
claims.innocentReading: The MoD guideline applied to every border state and every developer; SECI is a trading agency, not a builder, and wind-only was unviable; Adani was already the largest private allottee with adjacent land and evacuation capacity, making it the obvious taker. The base rate — how often Gujarat allots surrendered park land by competitive process — is unknown.
claims.upgradeIf: Records show other developers applied and were not considered, or that MNRE's instruction to SECI referenced Adani
claims.killIf: Records show SECI's surrender was decided before Adani's 3 July letter and the land was publicly offered

claims.lab: NTPC hybrid 1.2 GW: Adani 600 MW at ₹3.29/kWh (24 Oct 2024)
claims.d: Adani Renewable Energy won half of NTPC's 1,200 MW ISTS wind-solar hybrid auction at ₹3.29/kWh; Sembcorp 300 MW (₹3.29), Green Prairie 200 MW (₹3.28), Adyant Enersol 70 MW (₹3.28), ReNew 30 MW (₹3.29). Tariff spread of one paisa across winners.

benefit.how: 600 MW of 25-year hybrid PPAs won in a tariff-based auction; nothing in the record suggests non-price selection

claims.lab: NTPC hybrid: Sembcorp 300 MW at ₹3.29/kWh
claims.d: Sembcorp Green Infra won 300 MW in the same auction at the same tariff as Adani — the rival's take.

claims.lab: Concentration: top-5 developers ≈52% of 2024 commissioning; 59 GW auctioned
claims.d: 2024 auctions totalled 59 GW (2.3x 2023) with Avaada, JSW Energy and Adani Green the top winners; Mercom's 2024 leaderboard puts AGEL, ReNew, ACME, NTPC RE and O2 Power at ~52% of utility-scale commissioning. The market is concentrated but not single-firm: two of the three top 2024 winners (Avaada, JSW) are not Adani.
claims.innocentReading: Utility-scale RE has scale economies in land, evacuation and financing; concentration among 5–8 IPPs is the norm in comparable markets and the awards are tariff-based reverse auctions.
claims.upgradeIf: A full award register 2019–26 by awarder × winner shows a developer's share rising faster than its bid competitiveness

claims.lab: BESS VGF tranche-2: ₹5,400 cr for 30 GWh (10 Jun 2025)
claims.d: MoP approved ₹5,400 cr from the PSDF at ₹18 lakh/MWh for 30 GWh: 25 GWh across 15 states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra 4 GWh each) and 5 GWh to NTPC; 13.2 GWh already approved under tranche-1; commissioning within 18 months.

benefit.how: 5 GWh of VGF-backed storage allocated to a single PSU without competition; states must tender theirs

claims.lab: SECI Odisha BESS: Coal India 80 MW/320 MWh at ₹3.04–3.05 lakh/MW/month (2 Mar 2026)
claims.d: In SECI's 125 MW/500 MWh VGF-backed standalone BESS auction for Odisha (tender Dec 2025), Coal India won clusters I and II (40 MW/160 MWh each) at ₹3,04,000 and ₹3,05,000 per MW per month; Onward Solar Power 45 MW/180 MWh at ₹3,75,000; VGF capped at ₹18 lakh/MWh; 15-year O&M.

claims.lab: TNGECL 500 MW/1,000 MWh BESS: NLC India Renewables, Bondada, Oriana (24 Jun 2025)
claims.d: Tamil Nadu's own storage procurement: TNGECL's tender (floated March 2025) awarded across six sites on 2025-06-24 to NLC India Renewables, Bondada Engineering and Oriana Power; per-winner MW and tariffs not in the opened source.

claims.lab: PM Surya Ghar launched 15 Feb 2024; ₹75,021 cr outlay
claims.d: Rooftop subsidy scheme (up to ₹78,000 per household) launched 2024-02-15 targeting one crore households by FY27; 10 lakh installations reached 2025-03-10 with ₹4,770 cr disbursed to 6.13 lakh beneficiaries from 47.3 lakh applications. ALMM-listed (DCR) modules mandatory.

benefit.how: DCR requirement channels rooftop demand (12 GW+ by mid-2026 per trade press) to ALMM-listed domestic module makers; vendor-level shares are not published

claims.lab: Gujarat = 41.5% of the first 10 lakh rooftop installations
claims.d: At the 10-lakh mark (March 2025) Gujarat had 3,51,273 installations (41.47%), against UP 73,602 (8.69%) and Kerala 65,423 (7.73%). One BJP-ruled state absorbed two-fifths of a national subsidy in year one.
claims.innocentReading: Gujarat ran its own Surya Gujarat rooftop scheme from 2019 and had discom processes, vendor networks and net-metering already in place; the scheme is demand-driven, not allocated. Later data (trade press, not opened) show Maharashtra and UP catching up.
claims.upgradeIf: State-wise disbursement shows Gujarat's share persisting after other states' processes matured
claims.killIf: Gujarat's share falls toward its share of eligible households by 2026

claims.lab: PM-KUSUM: 34,800 MW target by 31 Mar 2026; CFA ₹34,422 cr
claims.d: Scheme components A/B/C with CFA 30% (50% special states) and feeder-level solarisation CFA up to ₹1.05 cr/MW; MNRE's page (updated 2025-11-07) publishes no achievement data.

claims.lab: PSA signatories 2021 spanned four parties; only AP is alleged to have been bribed
claims.d: States that signed SECI PSAs under the manufacturing-linked tender in 2021 were governed by YSRCP (AP, 7,000 MW), DMK (TN, 1,000 MW) and BJD (Odisha, 500 MW), with Chhattisgarh (INC) and J&K (UT) reported but not opened here. The indictment's bribery narrative centres on AP; the other buyers signed at the same ₹2.49 tariff without any such allegation.
claims.innocentReading: AP took roughly 7 of ~12 GW — a decision of a different order of magnitude than 0.5–1 GW, so the allegation's focus on AP is proportionate, not selective. Equally, four states signing at the same tariff is evidence the price was marketable without inducement.
claims.upgradeIf: Indictment exhibits or an Indian inquiry show inducements to any other state
claims.killIf: AP discoms' own filings show a tariff-based rationale identical to TN/Odisha's

narratives.claim: Adani bribed Andhra Pradesh officials to obtain the 7 GW SECI-linked offtake.
narratives.strongestCase: A US grand jury indictment and an SEC complaint allege it; AP's 7 GW PSA was signed 2021-12-01 shortly after the alleged promise; SECI could not find buyers at its rate; the Adanis paid $18m to settle the SEC's related securities-fraud claims; the FCPA count against Azure/CDPQ co-conspirators is still alive after the court twice refused to let DOJ drop it.
narratives.strongestCounter: The Adanis were never charged with bribery, only with misrepresenting anti-bribery practices; the criminal counts were dismissed with prejudice; the SEC settlement is without admission; three other states signed at the same ₹2.49 tariff without allegation; the rival TDP government, with every incentive, found no basis to cancel; no official is named and no Indian inquiry exists.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Trial or plea of any co-defendant; an Indian agency identifying the AP official; or dismissal of the FCPA count on the merits.

narratives.claim: Adani has been 'cleared' of the US bribery case.
narratives.strongestCase: Criminal counts against Gautam and Sagar Adani dismissed with prejudice (2026-08-10); SEC case settled; SEBI and CCI found nothing.
narratives.strongestCounter: Dismissal came on DOJ's own motion citing discretion, not on the merits; the judge said Indian documents were decisions not to investigate; SEBI's orders concern a different (Hindenburg RPT) matter; the FCPA conspiracy count against co-defendants remains pending as of Sept 2026.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A merits ruling on the FCPA count, or DOJ's refiled motion being granted.

narratives.claim: Defence rules on the Pakistan border were relaxed so Adani could take SECI's Khavda land.
narratives.strongestCase: Documented chronology: MoD relaxation Apr–May 2023 → Adani's requests 3 and 7 July → SECI surrender July (on ministerial instruction) → Adani Power selected 24 Aug without recorded bidding; Adani now holds more land than all others combined.
narratives.strongestCounter: The MoD guideline was general (all states, all developers); SECI is a trader not a builder and wind-only was unviable; Adani was already the adjacent largest private allottee; no document shows the relaxation was requested by or for Adani; Adani says it complied with policy.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Committee minutes or MNRE–SECI correspondence naming Adani before the surrender; or evidence of a public offer of the land.

narratives.claim: ALMM and PLI are protectionism designed for Adani.
narratives.strongestCase: Adani's Mundra Solar is on the ALMM lists and gains from List-II.
narratives.strongestCounter: PLI allocations went 10 GW each to Reliance and Shirdi Sai and only 0.7 GW to Adani (nothing in Tranche-II); ALMM List-I's biggest capacity is Waaree; List-II's first HJT entry is Reliance; the 2023–24 abeyance actually favoured importing developers over module makers.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Disbursement or list-inclusion data showing Adani-specific treatment.

narratives.claim: SECI's chairman was sacked to bury the Adani matter.
narratives.strongestCase: Timing (May 2025, six months after the indictment) and Gupta's public defence of SECI.
narratives.strongestCounter: The documented ground is SECI's acceptance of Reliance NU BESS's forged SBI guarantees, debarment and a police complaint of Oct 2024; termination came one month before scheduled tenure end.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: The ACC order or a file noting citing the US case.

symmetryCheck: Control 1 — Andhra Pradesh across two rival governments. The lens ('a government signs or protects a power contract that benefits a favoured developer') fires equally on YSRCP and TDP: the Jagan government (2019) tried to renegotiate Naidu-era wind/solar PPAs and lost in the High Court (2022, ~₹10,500 cr impact), then in 2021 signed the 7 GW SECI PSA now under allegation; the Naidu government, which had petitioned against that PSA in 2021, continued it in office after the indictment and secured APERC approval for FY26 purchases. Whichever party is in opposition attacks the PPA; whichever is in office honours it. That is a finding about discom economics and contract law, not about either party's probity. Control 2 — other 2021 PSA signatories: Tamil Nadu (DMK) and Odisha (BJD) signed at the identical ₹2.49 tariff with no allegation attached, and TN went on to run its own BESS auctions (NLC/Bondada/Oriana, June 2025) — the same procurement lens produces nothing alarming there. Control 3 — a rival group: the only SECI enforcement action against a developer in the record is the three-year debarment of Anil Ambani's Reliance Power for forged bank guarantees (Nov 2024), and the only SECI head removed was removed over that episode — the enforcement record points away from, not toward, Adani. Control 4 — PLI: the lens 'PLI favours the ruling party's presumed favourite' fails outright; Reliance and an obscure Andhra transformer maker took 41% of capacity and Adani 1.5%. Net: the lens over-fires on AP politics and under-fires on Adani in PLI; the one place it produces an asymmetric picture is Khavda land (61% of the park to one group after 2023 without recorded bidding), which is therefore where attention belongs.
